sections.label: Pallavi
sections.en: Lord Ganapathy, you are the chief of the army of ghosts; you are from the lineage of the Lord who adorns a moon on his matted locks.

sections.label: Anupallavi
sections.ta:
இமையவரும் போற்றிடும் இணையிலா ஈசனே
உமையவள் தன் உடலினின்று உதித்தவனே
sections.translit:
imaiyavarum pOtRidum iNaiyilA IsanE
umaiyavaL than udalinindRu udhitthavanE
sections.en: You are an incomparable Lord and all celestials sing your glory. You are born from Goddess Parvathi’s body.

sections.label: Charanam 1
sections.ta:
சுண்டெலி வாகனனே மோதக ப்ரியனே
ஆனை முகத்தோனே பானை வயிற்றோனே
தந்தைக்குபதேசம் செய்த கந்தனின் சோதரனே
தாயிற் சிறந்ததொரு கோயிலிலை என போதித்தவனே
sections.translit:
suNdeli vAgananE mOdhaga priyanE
Anai mugatthOnE pAnai vayitROnE
thandhaikkupadhEsam seydha kandhanin sOdharanE
thAyiR siRandhadhoru kOyililai ena bOdhitthavanE
sections.en: You ride a mouse as your vehicle; you are fond of caramelized sweet, modhakam; you possess an elephant face and have a pot belly; you are the brother of Kandhan who preached the inner meaning of the primordial sound Aum; you taught the universe the maxim that there is nothing more sacred than a mother.

sections.label: Charanam 2
sections.ta:
தொடங்கிடும் செயலனைத்தும் குவலயத்தில்
இடரின்றி நடந்திட துணைபுரியும் விக்னேஸ்வரனே
தந்தத்தை உடைத்தே அமலனின் கதையை
தடையின்றி முடித்த தயாபரனே
பரிபூர்ண விநாயகனே பதம் பிடித்தேன்
கரிசனையுடனே காத்தருள்வாயே
sections.translit:
thodangidum seyalanaitthum kuvalayatthil
idarindRi nadandhida thuNaipuriyum vignEsvaranE
thandhatthai udaitthE amalanin kadhaiyai
thadaiyindRi mudittha dhayAparanE
paripUrNa vinAyaganE padham piditthEn
karisanaiyudanE kAttharuLvAyE
sections.en: You ensure that all of the efforts by your  devotees proceed without obstacles. You acquired the name Vigneswaran. You are the compassionate one who helped to write the entire Mahabharata epic by breaking your own tusk and using it as the stylus for writing, as Sage Vyasa dictated. Oh, Paripoorna Vinyaka, I surrender at your divine feet. Please be considerate and protect me.

notes: This is the first song from my writings that Smt. Asha Ramesh tuned, rendering it as a prayer song in her concert at the Concord Siva Murugan Temple. The second charanam of the song traces how the great epic Mahabharata became a reality for posterity. Sage Vyasa conceived the divine tale of the Pandavas and Kauravas, encompassing the development of enmity between the relatives, the Kurukshetra war, Krishna’s advice to Arjuna on the battlefield, and the destruction that ensued. He invoked Lord Brahma, who suggested that he should pray to Lord Ganapathy before starting the work and seek his help for amanuensis. Sage Vyasa prayed to Ganesha and asked him to write down his dictations at the same speed as his narration. The five-handed Ganesha agreed on one condition: that Vyasa should not pause or break during the dictation. Vyasa suggested that Ganesha should write only what he was able to understand. Ganesha realized the immense task before him and broke his tusk and used the broken tusk as a quill to write and continued until the sacred tale was complete. The rest is history. Ganesha’s broken tusk is mythological and appears in Brahmanda Purana when Ganesha confronts Parasurama. In excessive anger, Parasurama threw his axe (which was given to him by Lord Siva) at Ganesha. Rather than duck and save himself, which would offend his dad (since he blessed the weapon), Ganesha accepted the axe which broke his tusk. Even though Veda Vyasa is accepted as the author of Brahmanda purana, researchers have concluded that several authors included insertions that were compiled much later. It is possible that a scribe during a later puranic time combined this incident into the origin story of the Mahabharata, with Ganesha using his broken tusk to scribe. For details, see: ஶ்ரீ மஹாபாரத ஸாரம், வேதவியாசர் அருளியது, உரை ஆசிரியர் “அண்ணா”, ஶ்ரீராமகிருஷ்ண மடம், மயிலாப்பூர், சென்னை 600004, பதிப்பு 2002 பக்கம் 3. Mahabharata, C.
